lead: Formal verification scales up, the public turns skeptical, and OpenAI's trillion-dollar ambitions meet investor resistance.

sections.title: Proof at production scale
sections.intro: A Theorem collaboration used Claude to formally verify security properties across 100+ open-source libraries at RISC-V assembly level, and CATT 0.2.1 brings assistant-emulation testing into CI - verification is becoming ordinary engineering.

sections.title: The public turns skeptical
sections.intro: A 57% majority of Americans now says AI is bad for society and two-thirds oppose new data centers, while Wall Street bristles at Meta's capital hunt and OpenAI trims its valuation target to $1.25T on investor resistance.

sections.title: Governance tightens its grip
sections.intro: The US Treasury proposed curbs on AI and supercomputing investment in countries of concern, a US appeals court ejected a judge over AI errors, and Anthropic formalized its Agent Skills donation with 70+ platforms aboard.

sections.title: Power follows compute
sections.intro: PreussenElektra and Nvidia are assessing Germany's idle nuclear plants as data-center sites, and an essay argues compute needs a real market like oil.

sections.title: Odd drops
sections.intro: a16z Crypto becomes a16z Frontier as the label chases AI, and JA Westenberg argues agency - not agents - is the scarce resource.

sections.title: Selling shovels or mining
sections.intro: An Ask HN debates why labs sell tokens instead of launching companies on their own models, and a fired-researchers leak story shows OpenAI's internal tensions over safety scrutiny.

sections.title: The build-out goes nuclear, literally
sections.intro: SK Hyper floats 15GW of Korean data centers with a $350B first phase, DeepSeek and MiniMax win Chinese approval to deploy overseas, and a per-request carbon method shows the same prompt emitting 8.5x more CO2 in Texas than Sweden.

sections.title: Odd drops
sections.intro: OnKey turns any song into a singing lesson with local pitch tracking on the Mac.
